title: Brazil votes with Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro leading the polls
summary:
Brazilians began voting on 4 October 2026 in a general election. Twelve candidates are running for president, but two familiar names lead the opinion polls: current president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and challenger Flávio Bolsonaro.

Lula represents the left-wing Workers’ Party. Flávio Bolsonaro is a right-wing politician and the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Left-wing and right-wing describe different political approaches to how a country should be governed.

Four years ago, Lula narrowly defeated Jair Bolsonaro. Jair Bolsonaro is not running this time. He is under house arrest following a conviction for plotting to overturn the election result, and restrictions prevent him from posting on social media or making public statements. However, the source reports that he backs his son’s campaign.

Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are the only candidates with support reaching double figures in the polls. Surveys suggest a second round of voting, called a run-off, is highly likely. However, many voters were still undecided shortly before election day, so a first-round victory remains possible.

Almost 160 million Brazilians are eligible to vote. People can vote from age 16. Voting is compulsory for people aged 18 to 70 who can read and write, and those who do not vote face a fine. Opinion polls usually question only thousands of people, so the final result may differ considerably from their predictions.

Lula, who is 80, has held the presidency three times. During his first two terms, from 2003 to 2010, he was widely praised for helping millions leave poverty through a cash-support programme called Bolsa Família. His later convictions for corruption and money laundering, which he has always denied, were annulled in 2021.

Environmental policy is another part of his record. Some environmentalists have criticised recent actions. Lula says oil income can help fund a move towards clean energy and that he remains committed to eventually ending fossil-fuel use. His government points to satellite data suggesting Amazon deforestation in the first half of 2026 fell to its lowest level in a decade.
why_it_matters: The election will choose Brazil’s president, with almost 160 million people eligible to vote. The article helps readers distinguish poll predictions from results and consider the candidates’ backgrounds and records.
